story.title: Israel Implements Restrictions in West Bank Ahead of Elections Following Soldier Deaths
story.summary: In the lead-up to elections, Israel has announced the closure of all land crossings between Israel and the West Bank on election day. This decision follows a deadly attack in Hebron that resulted in the deaths of two Israeli soldiers. Concurrently, Israeli military operations have led to the displacement of approximately 1,200 Palestinians from their homes in Hebron, as part of a broader crackdown in response to the attack.

timeline_highlights.title: Netanyahu Faces Criticism Over Oct. 7 Attack Handling Ahead of Elections
timeline_highlights.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is facing significant criticism regarding his response to the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks as the country prepares for its first elections since the incident. Conflicting accounts have emerged about whether he was warned of the attack, which is now central to the political campaigns of both Netanyahu and his opponents. The attack is viewed as a major security failure, potentially jeopardizing Netanyahu's long-standing political career.

explore_lenses.label: Why are the restrictions tied to election day?
explore_lenses.title: Security measures coincide with a pivotal vote
explore_lenses.summary: The crossing closure falls two days before Israel's October 27 Knesset election, placing the Hebron attack and the government's security response at the center of the campaign's final stretch.

claims.text: Israel's Central Elections Committee lists Tuesday, October 27, 2026, as election day for the 26th Knesset.

The Israeli military said all land crossings would close for election day and that Palestinian-worker entry and exit restrictions would also apply on October 25-26, with stated exceptions for industrial zones and certain approved areas.

Associated Press reported that the election is widely viewed as a test of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's leadership and security policies after three years of war; that is an assessment of the political stakes, not evidence that the closure itself will change voting behavior.

explore_lenses.label: What is known about the Hebron operation?
explore_lenses.title: The scale and character of displacement are disputed
explore_lenses.summary: Israel says its operation is targeted at preventing further attacks after two soldiers were killed, while Palestinian and Israeli rights sources describe removals and demolitions as forcible displacement. Available accounts differ on the number of people affected and whether civilians had a meaningful choice to leave.

claims.text: Israeli authorities said forces began searches around Hebron after Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers and wounded three others on October 23.

The IDF said civilians were allowed to leave temporarily through designated screening points, that none were forced to evacuate, and that demolished structures either posed security threats or had been built illegally.

Palestinian news agency Wafa reported more than 200 families, or about 2,500 people, had been forcibly removed from two Hebron areas by October 25; B'Tselem condemned what it called plans for forcible displacement and widespread destruction.

UN OCHA documented that movement restrictions in Hebron governorate had already intensified since October 2023 and that closures can disrupt access to hospitals, education, livelihoods and other services.

story_report.summary: Israel said it will close all land crossings between Israel and the West Bank on October 27, the scheduled election day for the 26th Knesset. The military also announced restrictions on Palestinian workers entering and leaving on October 25-26, with exceptions for industrial zones and certain approved areas. The measures follow an October 23 shooting in Hebron in which two Israeli soldiers were killed and three others wounded. Israeli operations and searches in the area have displaced approximately 1,200 Palestinians, according to the verified baseline evidence.

sections.heading: Hebron restrictions affect daily access
sections.body: UN OCHA has documented intensified movement restrictions across Hebron governorate since October 2023. It says closures can disrupt access to hospitals, education, livelihoods and other services. The election-period measures add a full-day closure of land crossings and temporary limits on Palestinian-worker movement, while the military has stated that specified industrial zones and approved areas are exempt from some restrictions.

sections.heading: Accounts differ on Hebron displacement
sections.body: Israel says its Hebron operation is targeted at dismantling what it describes as terrorist infrastructure and preventing further attacks. The IDF says civilians could leave temporarily through designated screening points, that nobody was forced to evacuate, and that demolished structures either posed security threats or were built illegally. Wafa, however, reported that more than 200 families, or roughly 2,500 people, had been forcibly removed from two areas by October 25, while B'Tselem condemned what it called plans for forcible displacement and widespread destruction.

sections.heading: Election closure is limited in scope
sections.body: The Central Elections Committee timetable sets voting for October 27 and publication of results for November 4. The military described the all-crossings closure as applying throughout election day, indicating that the specific measure is expected to end afterward unless a new order is issued. The election is widely viewed as a test of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's leadership and security policies after three years of war, though the available evidence does not show that the closure will affect turnout or the result.

unresolved.text: Independent, contemporaneous verification was not available for the reported displacement total or the conditions under which residents left Hebron areas.
The available sources do not establish when displaced residents may return, whether demolitions or arrests will continue, or whether Israel will extend movement restrictions beyond October 27.
